allowed.reason: ACL order only. 20261102100100 revokes EXECUTE from PUBLIC, anon and authenticated, then grants it to authenticated and service_role. Under the managed default privilege hosted is recorded to have (postgres in public grants EXECUTE on new functions to anon, authenticated and service_role; COORDINATION.md, 'default privileges'), service_role keeps its default grant and authenticated is re-added after it, so the ACL reads postgres, service_role, authenticated. Without that default it reads postgres, authenticated, service_role. Lane 09 rehearsal, 2026-11-14: two dry runs of the same plan on one stand-in, before and after adding that default privilege, differed in this key alone. If the restored copy carries hosted's default privileges, as a full pg_dump should, this entry goes unused. What this entry covers and what it does not: the key's value is a hash of the function's body, owner, ACL, settings, security, volatility and parallel mode (catalog_keys.sql), and allowing the key lets any of them differ between the restored copy and hosted. The body, settings, security, volatility and parallel mode come from the file pinned by its SHA-256 in plan.template.json and are checked again by the definition hash in postchecks.sql; the ACL is checked in postchecks.sql (anon refused, authenticated and service_role allowed); the owner is checked in postchecks.sql (postgres). So only the order of the ACL entries goes unchecked. Every other key, including the other nine functions the seven files create or replace, must still match the restored copy exactly.
